## Berlin 1-Bedroom Shortlist for Your Move

You want a **1-bedroom for 2 adults**, keep rent at **€1,800/month all-in**, and stay near a **30-minute commute to Alexanderplatz**. Based on that, **Moabit is the strongest fit**, with Neukölln a close budget-safe backup.

## Best-to-Worst Comparison

| Rank | Listing | Rent | Size | Commute to Alexanderplatz | Lease | Pets | Fit for You |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Moabit | €1,700 | 60 m² | 28 min | 6-month lease | Yes | Best overall balance |
| 2 | Neukölln | €1,650 | 52 m² | 35 min | 12-month lease | Yes | Best budget stability |
| 3 | Prenzlauer Berg | €1,850 | 48 m² | 22 min | Unfurnished | No | Fast commute, but over budget |

## Why This Ranking Works

### 1) Moabit — Best overall fit
- **Within budget**: €1,700 leaves **€100/month buffer**
- **Commute matches your target**: **28 min** is right on goal
- **Most space**: **60 m²** is the most comfortable for 2 adults
- **Good flexibility**: furnished + pets allowed

Main downside:
- **Only a 6-month lease**, so it is less stable if you want a longer stay
- You may need to plan a renewal or a second move sooner than ideal

### 2) Neukölln — Best budget-safe long-term option
- **Cheapest option** at **€1,650**
- **12-month lease** is the most secure of the three
- **Pets allowed**
- Good size at **52 m²**

Main downside:
- **35-minute commute** misses your 30-minute target
- **Unfurnished** means higher move-in costs and more setup effort

### 3) Prenzlauer Berg — Best location, weakest financial fit
- **Fastest commute** at **22 minutes**
- Solid central location appeal

Main downsides:
- **Over budget** at **€1,850**
- **No pets**
- **Unfurnished**
- Smaller at **48 m²**

## Best Tradeoffs to Make

If you want to stay **under €1,800/month**, the most sensible compromises are:

- **Compromise on lease length** if you want the best overall apartment: take **Moabit** and accept the **6-month lease**
- **Compromise on commute time** if you want stability: take **Neukölln** and accept the **35-minute commute**
- **Do not compromise on budget** if “all-in” is strict: **Prenzlauer Berg is over your cap**, so it is the weakest financial fit

## Recommendation

**Best fit: Moabit**
- It gives you the best mix of **budget, commute, size, and comfort**
- The only major drawback is the **short lease**
- If you can handle possible renewal uncertainty, this is the strongest choice for your situation

**Best conservative backup: Neukölln**
- Choose this if you value **lease stability** more than hitting the commute target exactly

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Compare commute options] https://www.bvg.de/en
Action: [Button: Check district rental market] https://www.immobilienscout24.de/
Action: [Button: Plan route to Alexanderplatz] https://www.google.com/maps

## Sources

- Berlin public transit planner: https://www.bvg.de/en
- Berlin rental market listings: https://www.immobilienscout24.de/
- Route planning: https://www.google.com/maps

## Friday Movie Night Fit
For **2 adults + 1 teen**, the best fit is the one that stays **light, PG-13 friendly, low on violence, and under 120 minutes**. I ranked these with that balance in mind.

## Top 3 Picks
| Rank | Film | Why it fits |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Paper Stars** | Shortest option with a light rom-com tone, so it best matches a fun, easy Friday-night mood with minimal heavy content. |
| 2 | **Galaxy Heist** | The sci-fi comedy angle gives you humor and energy while staying more playful than intense, though it runs a little long. |
| 3 | **Dragon Lantern** | Adventure and fantasy usually make for a crowd-pleasing family pick, with enough excitement to be fun but typically less bleak than the thriller or drama options. |

## Best-Fit Ranking Notes
- **Paper Stars** — Best overall because it is **under 90 minutes** and likely the least emotionally heavy option.
- **Galaxy Heist** — Strong second choice if you want **more laughs and a bigger crowd-pleaser**, with the main drawback being the **122-minute** runtime.
- **Dragon Lantern** — Good backup pick for a more “movie-night” feel; it should be **bright, imaginative, and teen-friendly**.
- **Summer Circuit** — Likely gentler than the action/thriller picks, but “coming-of-age drama” can skew more sad or reflective than you want.
- **Midnight Harbor** — Mystery thrillers often bring tension and darker moments, so it is less ideal for a light night.
- **Iron Relay** — Most likely to feature the **most violence and intensity**, plus it is the longest.

## Watch-Order Recommendation
1. **Paper Stars** — safest bet for a light, upbeat evening
2. **Galaxy Heist** — best if you want more laughs and spectacle
3. **Dragon Lantern** — best alternate if you want a more adventurous vibe

## Quick Actions
- If you want the **safest pick for mixed ages**: choose **Paper Stars**
- If you want the **most fun and energetic pick**: choose **Galaxy Heist**
- If you want the **best fantasy-family-style option**: choose **Dragon Lantern**

## Best Robot Vacuum for a 1,200 sq ft Cat Apartment

For your priorities — **pet hair pickup**, **low maintenance**, then **quiet operation** — the best fit is **CleanBot S8**. It stays under budget, has a self-empty base, and offers enough suction/runtime for a 1,200 sq ft hardwood apartment with two cats.

## Ranked Comparison

| Rank | Model | Price | Pet Hair Pickup | Maintenance | Quietness | Fit for You |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CleanBot S8 | $399 | Strong | Very low | متوسط | Best overall balance |
| 2 | DustAway X2 | $449 | Decent | Very low | Best | Quietest, but weaker pickup |
| 3 | SweepMax Pro | $349 | Best suction | Higher | متوسط | Strong cleaning, more upkeep |

### Why each ranks where it does

**1) CleanBot S8**
- **Why it wins:** self-empty base + solid suction + long runtime makes it the easiest daily driver for cat hair.
- **Trade-off:** not the quietest option, but it is quieter than many high-suction models in practice.
- **Best for:** hands-off cleaning with strong all-around performance.

**2) DustAway X2**
- **Why it’s close:** self-empty base and **quiet mode** are excellent for low maintenance and noise-sensitive use.
- **Trade-off:** lower suction than the others, so it is less compelling for heavier pet hair buildup.
- **Best for:** if quiet operation mattered more than pickup strength.

**3) SweepMax Pro**
- **Why it trails:** best raw suction and lowest price, plus mopping is nice on hardwood.
- **Trade-off:** no self-empty base means more frequent bin emptying, which conflicts with your low-maintenance priority.
- **Best for:** if you want maximum suction per dollar and don’t mind more upkeep.

## Best Pick Under Budget

**Choose: CleanBot S8**
- **Price:** $399
- **Why it fits your priorities:**
  - Good pet hair pickup
  - Self-empty base for low maintenance
  - Enough runtime for 1,200 sq ft in one pass
- **Budget check:** comfortably under your **$450** cap

## Quick Actions

response_text:
## Barcelona Family Stay at a Glance
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

For a 4-night family stay, **all four options stay under your €1,100 lodging budget**.
Given your priorities, **Sagrada Suites** is the strongest match for comfort and rollaway-bed potential, while **Hotel Alba** is the best value-balanced choice.

## Option Comparison and Best Fit

| Option | 4-night total | Neighborhood | Breakfast | Rollaway-bed fit | Metro walk | Cancellation | Overall fit |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Hotel Alba | €840 | Eixample | Included | Good, but a bit snug at 24 m² | 4 min | Free cancellation | Strong value |
| Casa Mar | €740 | Gothic Quarter | Not included | Good space at 28 m² | 2 min | No free cancellation | Cheapest, but misses key needs |
| Sagrada Suites | €980 | Gràcia | Included | Best fit; family room available at 26 m² | 6 min | Free cancellation | **Best overall** |
| Port View Inn | €780 | Barceloneta | Included | Tight at 22 m² | 8 min | Free cancellation | Budget-friendly, but least roomy |

### My recommendation
- **Best overall fit:** **Sagrada Suites**
  - Quiet, family-friendly **Gràcia** location
  - **Breakfast included**
  - **Family room available** makes the rollaway-bed request much more realistic
  - Still within budget at **€980**
- **Safest value:** **Hotel Alba**
  - Strong balance of **Eixample**, breakfast, free cancellation, and metro access
  - Lower cost than Sagrada Suites, while still feeling safe and convenient
  - Best if you want a bit more budget cushion for meals, transit, or incidentals
- **Best budget fit:** **Hotel Alba**
  - It’s the best blend of price and practicality
  - Total stays comfortably under budget at **€840**
  - Better fit than Casa Mar because it includes breakfast and free cancellation

### Why I would not pick the others
- **Casa Mar** is the cheapest, but breakfast is extra and there’s **no free cancellation**.
- **Port View Inn** is reasonable on price, but **22 m²** is tight for 2 adults + 1 child + rollaway bed.

## Booking Checklist Before You Pay
- Confirm the **final total** includes taxes, city tax, and breakfast.
- Ask whether a **rollaway bed is allowed** in the booked room type and whether there is an extra fee.
- Request a **quiet room** away from the elevator, street, and service areas.
- Verify the **child policy** for a 9-year-old and whether bedding is included or separate.
- Check the **cancellation deadline** and whether the booking is prepaid or pay-at-property.
- Make sure the room can physically handle **3 sleepers plus luggage** without feeling cramped.
- If choosing **Casa Mar**, confirm breakfast cost and cancellation terms before booking.

## Sources
- Barcelona Metro: https://www.tmb.cat/en/barcelona-metro
- Barcelona neighborhoods and city areas: https://www.barcelona.cat/en/what-to-do-in-bcn/neighbourhoods
- Barcelona tourism: https://www.barcelonaturisme.com/wv3/en/

## 2025 H1 E-Commerce Dashboard Brief

**Executive view**
- **Total revenue:** **$274,000**
- **Total orders:** **5,310**
- **Total returns:** **218**
- **Overall return rate:** **4.10%**
- **Revenue change Jan → Jun:** **+17.9%**

## Recommended Chart Stack

| Visualization | Chart type | Axes | Main takeaway |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue trend | Line chart | X: Month; Y: Revenue_USD | Shows steady growth from **$42,000** in Jan to a peak of **$51,000** in May, with a slight dip in June. |
| Order volume and returns | Combo chart: bars for Orders, line for Returns | X: Month; Y-left: Orders; Y-right: Returns | Shows demand rising through May while returns also increase, helping the manager spot operating pressure alongside growth. |
| Return rate by month | Line chart of derived metric | X: Month; Y: Return Rate % = Returns / Orders | Highlights quality/control changes over time; useful for spotting months where returns rose faster than order growth. |

## Key Readouts and Outliers

- **Best revenue month:** **May 2025** at **$51,000**
- **Highest order volume:** **May 2025** with **980 orders**
- **Highest return count:** **May 2025** with **44 returns**
- **Highest return rate:** **April 2025** at **4.51%**
- **Unusual month:** **April 2025** stands out because returns jump to the highest rate even though revenue continues to grow.

## 4 Concise Insights

- Revenue grew **17.9%** from January to June, with a clear upward trend overall.
- Orders increased from **820** to **980**, then eased slightly in June, suggesting demand stayed strong but softened at the end of the period.
- Returns remained relatively stable, but the **return rate rose in April and May**, which may indicate fulfillment or product-quality pressure.
- **April is the clearest outlier**: it has the **highest return rate** despite healthy revenue, so it deserves a closer operational review.

response_text:
# Kyoto Solo Trip Plan: 2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13

A relaxed, transit-first plan built around late starts, clustered neighborhoods, and one long lunch break each day. I’m treating this as **3 hotel nights / 4 sightseeing days**, with a total on-the-ground budget cap of **¥85,000** excluding flights.

## 4-Day Route at a Glance

| Day | Core Area | Main Focus | Transit Approach | Est. Steps | Day Budget |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Apr 10 | Higashiyama / Gion | Temples + first evening walk | Subway + short bus; keep one taxi option for uphill return | 13k–15k | ¥20,500 |
| Apr 11 | Central Kyoto | **Nishiki Market** + temple time | Subway + walkable blocks around Karasuma/Gion | 11k–14k | ¥22,000 |
| Apr 12 | North Kyoto | Temple complex + **low-key neighborhood walk** | Keihan/Subway + one bus link if needed | 12k–15k | ¥21,000 |
| Apr 13 | Arashiyama / Kyoto Station | Riverside temple morning + farewell dinner | JR or Hankyu; minimal transfers | 13k–16k | ¥21,500 |

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: East Kyoto soft start
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive slowly after **10:00**; settle in, then head to **Yasaka Shrine** and Maruyama Park for an easy first loop.
- **Long lunch:** **12:00–13:30** in Gion or near Higashiyama; sit down and fully rest before the temple walk.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** after the biggest early crush has passed, then wander **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka** at an unhurried pace.
- **Evening activity:** A quiet **Gion Shirakawa** stroll and early dinner.
- **Rainy-day backup:** **Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art** plus café time in Okazaki.
- **Pace target:** about **13k–15k steps**.

### Day 2: Nishiki Market and central Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Start after **10:00** at **Nishiki Market** so you miss the earliest lunch rush; keep it to a tasting walk, not a full meal.
- **Long lunch:** **12:30–14:00** in a café or teishoku spot near Karasuma so your feet get a real break.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Kennin-ji** and then drift through the quieter back lanes of Gion.
- **Evening activity:** Dinner in **Pontocho** or a low-key bar/tea stop nearby.
- **Rainy-day backup:** **Kyoto International Manga Museum** and the covered Teramachi/Kawaramachi arcades.
- **Pace target:** about **11k–14k steps**.

### Day 3: North Kyoto neighborhood walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Head north after **10:00** to the **Daitoku-ji** area for a temple-focused start without the biggest crowds.
- **Long lunch:** **12:00–13:30** in **Nishijin** or around Imadegawa; treat this as a proper sit-down break.
- **Afternoon:** Do your **low-key neighborhood walk** through **Nishijin** and nearby side streets, then add **Kitano Tenmangu** if you still feel fresh.
- **Evening activity:** **Kamo River** sunset walk, then dinner in a simple izakaya near Demachiyanagi.
- **Rainy-day backup:** **Nishijin Textile Center** and a long coffee stop.
- **Pace target:** about **12k–15k steps**.

### Day 4: Arashiyama with a late start
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- **Morning:** Take **JR or Hankyu** to **Arashiyama** and arrive after **10:00**; visit **Tenryu-ji** first, then keep the riverside walk compact.
- **Long lunch:** **12:00–13:45** with yudofu, soba, or another sit-down meal in Arashiyama.
- **Afternoon:** Choose **one** extra stop only: **Okochi Sanso** gardens or a short Sagano edge walk.
- **Evening activity:** A farewell dinner near **Kyoto Station** or downtown Kyoto.
- **Rainy-day backup:** **Kyoto Railway Museum** or **Kyoto Aquarium**.
- **Pace target:** about **13k–16k steps**.

## Budget, Transit, and Pace Control

- **Transit approach:** Use an **ICOCA/Suica** card, then lean on **subway + Keihan + JR/Hankyu** for the main moves. Use buses only for the last mile or very direct temple links.
- **Crowd control:** Put the most popular sights **after 10:00**, and keep each day to **two clustered areas max**.
- **Step control:** If a route adds steep walking or a long transfer, swap in one short taxi ride rather than forcing a 20-minute uphill walk.
- **Budget shape:** Keep **food + entry + local transit** around **¥6,000–9,000/day**, with your hotel bringing the trip into the **¥85,000** cap.

## Spring Packing Checklist

- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Compact umbrella or rain shell
- Comfortable walking shoes with good cushioning
- Socks you can change mid-day if it rains
- Small crossbody bag or daypack
- Portable charger
- Refillable water bottle
- A scarf or thin layer for temple interiors and breezy nights
- Cash and IC card for small purchases and transit

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Kyoto Official Travel] https://kyoto.travel/en
Action: [Button: Kyoto Transit Info] https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/
Action: [Button: Nishiki Market] https://www.nishiki.or.jp/en/

## Sources

- Kyoto Official Travel Guide: https://kyoto.travel/en
- Kyoto City Transportation Bureau: https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/
- Nishiki Market Association: https://www.nishiki.or.jp/en/

## 30-Minute Dinner at a Glance
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

A fast stovetop chicken-and-rice dinner with chickpeas, tomatoes, and spinach.
I’m assuming you also have **salt, pepper, 1 tbsp oil, and 2 cups water** for the rice.

**Ingredient list for 2**
- 2 chicken breasts, cut into bite-size pieces
- 1 can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
- 3 cups spinach
- 2 tomatoes, diced
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 cup rice
- 1/2 cup plain yogurt
- 1 tbsp oil
- Salt and pepper

## Fast Stovetop Method
1. **Cook the rice:** Rinse the rice, then simmer it with **2 cups water** and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, cover, then cook on low for about **15 minutes**.
2. **Brown the chicken:** While the rice cooks, heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season chicken with salt and pepper, then cook for **5-6 minutes** until lightly browned.
3. **Add garlic and tomatoes:** Stir in the garlic and tomatoes. Cook for **2 minutes** until fragrant and juicy.
4. **Mix in chickpeas:** Add the chickpeas plus a small splash of water. Cook for **3-4 minutes** to warm through.
5. **Wilt the spinach:** Add the spinach and stir until just wilted, about **1-2 minutes**.
6. **Finish with yogurt:** Turn off the heat. Stir in the yogurt off heat for a creamy sauce, or spoon it over each bowl to keep it fresh and tangy.
7. **Serve:** Spoon the chicken mixture over the rice and serve right away.

## Nutrition Per Serving
Using the amounts above, each serving is approximately:
- **Calories:** 700-850
- **Protein:** 45-60 g

## Lactose-Free Swap
- Use **lactose-free plain yogurt** in the same amount instead of regular yogurt.

# Porto First-Time 3-Day Walking Plan

Two adults, staying near **Ribeira**, with a calm pace, short transit help on day 3, and a combined non-hotel budget of **€240**. I’m treating that budget as food, local transit, and admissions for the trip; this plan keeps most days around **8,000–11,500 steps**.

## Route, Pace, and Budget Fit

| Day | Focus | Main walking pattern | Est. steps | Budget target |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Ribeira + Sé + riverfront viewpoints | Short loops from Ribeira, mostly flat with one gentle uphill | 7,500–9,000 | €70 |
| 2 | Baixa + Clérigos + bookshop streets | City-center loop with a few steeper streets; use café breaks | 9,000–10,500 | €85 |
| 3 | Gaia viewpoints + easy riverside finish | Short transit hop to save steps; scenic walking on both banks | 8,500–11,000 | €85 |

Trip note: to stay inside **€240**, aim for **1 paid attraction per day**, simple lunches, and one nicer dinner only if you skip an extra ticketed stop.

## Day 1: Ribeira, Sé, and the Riverfront

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- **Morning:** Start in **Ribeira** and walk the quay, then take the 10–15 min uphill route to **Porto Cathedral (Sé)**. Keep it slow and photo-friendly; expect about **2,500–3,000 steps**.
- **Afternoon:** Continue to **São Bento Station**, then through the historic lanes toward **Rua das Flores** and **Miradouro da Vitória**. Total walking: **45–60 min** spread out, about **3,000–3,500 steps**.
- **Evening:** Cross toward the lower bridge area for sunset views, then return to Ribeira for dinner. Keep the bridge-side loop to **30–40 min** so the day stays under **9,000 steps**.
- **Food:** Choose a classic riverside dinner: **bacalhau**, grilled sardines, or a simple **petiscos** share plate.
- **Rainy backup:** **Igreja de São Francisco + Porto Cathedral cloisters + café time in Baixa**.

## Day 2: Baixa, Clérigos, and the Bookshop Streets

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

- **Morning:** Walk 10 min to **São Bento** if you want a second look, then continue through **Avenida dos Aliados** and the old commercial streets. Plan **45 min of walking** before your first coffee stop.
- **Afternoon:** Head uphill to **Torre dos Clérigos**, the **Lello area**, and **Carmo/Carmelitas**; use a slow circuit so the climb feels manageable. Expect **60–90 min total** with breaks and roughly **4,000 steps**.
- **Evening:** Have an early dinner around **Praça dos Poveiros** or back near Baixa, then finish with an easy night stroll only if you still feel fresh. Keep the evening walk to **20–25 min**.
- **Food:** Go for a **francesinha** at lunch or share one at dinner, then add a pastel de nata or rice pudding later.
- **Rainy backup:** **Livraria Lello timed visit + Church of Carmo + Museu Nacional Soares dos Reis**.

## Day 3: Gaia Viewpoints and an Easy Riverside Finish

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg

- **Morning:** Take a short transit hop from Ribeira to **Jardim do Morro / Gaia** so you save your legs for the views; walk the upper terrace and bridge approaches. Transit/walk time: **20–30 min ride + 30–40 min on foot**.
- **Afternoon:** Descend toward the riverfront for a relaxed lunch and a slow promenade along the Gaia quays; this is the best day for port-wine scenery without racking up steps. Plan **60–75 min walking** plus sit-down time.
- **Evening:** Finish at **Serra do Pilar** or a similar viewpoint for golden-hour city views, then return to Ribeira for a final dinner. Keep the last walking segment to **15–25 min**.
- **Food:** Try **port wine** after dinner, plus a simpler local dish earlier so the day stays within budget.
- **Rainy backup:** **Port wine cellar visit + indoor tasting + a riverside lunch stop**.

## Practical Neighborhood Tips for Getting Around

- **Ribeira is the easiest base** for your plan, but the streets are narrow and busy at sunset; leave extra time for dinner reservations and bridge crossings.
- **Wear grippy shoes.** Porto’s cobblestones and slopes are the real challenge, not distance.
- **Use short transit strategically:** a bus, metro, or funicular on day 3 saves steps for the scenic parts.
- **Plan uphill sections before lunch** when you have more energy; save the riverfront strolls for late afternoon and evening.
- **Keep an eye on phones and wallets** in crowded areas like São Bento, viewpoints, and tram stops.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Porto transit map] https://www.metrodoporto.pt/
Action: [Button: Visit Porto] https://visitporto.travel/

## Sources

- Porto tourism office: https://visitporto.travel/
- Metro do Porto: https://www.metrodoporto.pt/
- STCP buses: https://www.stcp.pt/

response_text:
# Why this is probably happening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

Because **other devices connect normally** and your XPS 13 can **see** the SSID, this looks more like a **Wi‑Fi compatibility issue** than a broken laptop. The most likely culprits are:

- **WPA3 / PMF / security-mode mismatch** on the new TP-Link router
- **Wi‑Fi 6 (802.11ax)**, **160 MHz**, or **band steering/Smart Connect** causing the Dell to connect briefly and then drop
- **Intel Wi‑Fi adapter power-saving or roaming settings** in Windows
- Less likely: a corrupted Windows network stack or DHCP lease issue

# Prioritized troubleshooting checklist

| Priority | Action | What to check | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | On the **Archer AX55**, temporarily set security to **WPA2-Personal (AES)** only; turn **off WPA3**, **PMF required**, **Smart Connect**, **160 MHz**, and **802.11ax/Wi‑Fi 6** for a test. | Can the XPS connect and stay connected for 10+ minutes? | If yes, the issue is router compatibility, not the laptop. |
| 2 | On the Dell, open **Device Manager > Network adapters > Intel Wi‑Fi** > **Properties**. | **Power Management** and **Advanced** settings. | The adapter should stop dropping after tuning. |
| 3 | Split the router into two SSIDs: one for **2.4 GHz** and one for **5 GHz**. Test each band separately. | Does one band work while the other fails? | If one band is stable, the problem is band-specific. |
| 4 | Set the AX55 **5 GHz channel** to a non-DFS channel and **channel width** to **80 MHz**. | Avoid **Auto** / **160 MHz** for now. | The laptop should stop disconnecting shortly after join. |
| 5 | Use **Windows Network reset** before any full PC reset. | `Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset` | Fresh network stack after reboot, without wiping the PC. |
| 6 | Update the **AX55 firmware** and, if needed, test the laptop on a **phone hotspot**. | Compare hotspot vs home Wi‑Fi behavior. | If hotspot is stable, the router settings are the likely cause. |

# Windows 11 settings to verify
- `Settings > Network & internet > Wi‑Fi > Manage known networks > your SSID`
  - **Random hardware addresses** = **Off**
- `Settings > Network & internet > Proxy`
  - **Use a proxy server** = **Off**
- `Device Manager > Network adapters > Intel Wi‑Fi 6/Intel Wireless`
  - `Properties > Power Management`
    - Uncheck **Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power**
- `Device Manager > Network adapters > Intel Wi‑Fi 6/Intel Wireless`
  - `Properties > Advanced`
    - **802.11ax Mode** = **Disabled** for testing
    - **Preferred Band** = **Prefer 5 GHz**; if still unstable, test **Prefer 2.4 GHz**
    - **Channel Width for 5 GHz** = **80 MHz**
    - **Roaming Aggressiveness** = **Lowest** or **Medium-Low**
    - **Transmit Power** = **Highest**
- `Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings`
  - **Network reset** = use this **before** any whole-PC reset

**Fastest likely fix:** make the AX55 more compatible first — **WPA2-only + Wi‑Fi 6 off + Smart Connect off + 80 MHz on 5 GHz** — then retest the laptop.

# Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Windows network reset] https://support.microsoft.com/windows
Action: [Button: TP-Link AX55 support] https://www.tp-link.com/us/support/download/archer-ax55/
Action: [Button: Dell support home] https://www.dell.com/support/home

# Sources
- Microsoft Windows support: https://support.microsoft.com/windows
- TP-Link Archer AX55 support/downloads: https://www.tp-link.com/us/support/download/archer-ax55/
- Dell support home: https://www.dell.com/support/home

## Cover Letter Draft

## Ready-to-Send Letter

Dear Hiring Manager,

I’m excited to apply for the Mid-Level Product Analyst role in Berlin. With 4 years of experience in SQL, Tableau, A/B testing, and stakeholder reporting, I’ve learned how to turn data into decisions that are practical, measurable, and easy for teams to act on. I’m now looking to bring that approach into SaaS product analytics as I relocate to Berlin in September 2026.

In my current retail analytics role, I led reporting and experimentation work that helped improve a key conversion funnel by **12%** over two quarters. I also built a Tableau reporting layer that cut weekly stakeholder reporting time by **40%**, giving business teams faster access to the metrics they needed. Across both projects, I focused on clean analysis, clear communication, and recommendations that could be implemented without delay.

What appeals to me about SaaS companies is the pace of learning and the direct link between product decisions and customer outcomes. I enjoy working in environments where small improvements can have a visible effect on retention, activation, and revenue. The chance to help a product team understand user behavior, test hypotheses, and refine the experience based on evidence is exactly the kind of work I want to do next.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my analytics background, experimentation experience, and stakeholder-facing communication can support your product team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

## Notes for Personalization

- Replace the company name in the greeting if you have it.
- If you want, I can also tailor this into a version for a specific Berlin SaaS company or make it sound slightly warmer or more direct.

# Toronto Household Spending Review, Jan–Jun 2024

**Context for the analysis:** I treated each row as one family-month in CAD and calculated monthly totals, category shares, and month-over-month changes.

## Monthly Spend Trend

**Formula:** `Total monthly spend = Rent + Groceries + Transport + Utilities + EatingOut + Misc`

| Month | Total Spend | MoM Change | MoM % | Notable shift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2024-01 | CAD 3,700 | Base month | — | Rent dominates the budget |
| 2024-02 | CAD 3,745 | +CAD 45 | +1.2% | Groceries and eating out both rose |
| 2024-03 | CAD 3,810 | +CAD 65 | +1.7% | Groceries kept climbing |
| 2024-04 | CAD 3,900 | +CAD 90 | +2.4% | Largest jump; eating out rose sharply |
| 2024-05 | CAD 3,910 | +CAD 10 | +0.3% | Smallest increase; groceries dipped slightly |
| 2024-06 | CAD 3,985 | +CAD 75 | +1.9% | Highest month in the period |

**Period totals**
- **6-month total spend:** **CAD 23,050**
- **Average monthly spend:** **CAD 3,842**
- **Jan to Jun change:** **+CAD 285** (**+7.7%**)

## Cost Drivers Behind the Budget

**Top three cost drivers over the 6 months**
- **Rent:** **CAD 13,200** total, about **57.3%** of all spending
- **Groceries:** **CAD 4,150** total, about **18.0%**
- **Eating out:** **CAD 2,250** total, about **9.8%**

**What the pattern says**
- **Rent is the anchor cost** and is completely stable at CAD 2,200 per month.
- **Groceries are drifting upward** from CAD 640 to CAD 730, suggesting inflation, larger basket sizes, or less strict shopping control.
- **Eating out is the clearest growth category**, rising every month from CAD 320 to CAD 430.
- **Utilities and transport are fairly controlled**, with only modest increases.

## Three Cuts to Reduce Spending by 8%+

To avoid changing **rent** or **transport**, focus on the flexible categories.
A realistic target is **about CAD 312/month** in savings, which is **8.1%** of the average monthly spend.

1. **Cap eating out at CAD 240/month**
   - Current average: **CAD 375**
   - Target savings: **CAD 135/month**
   - How: set a restaurant budget, use 2–3 more home-cooked dinners each week, and reserve eating out for planned occasions.

2. **Bring groceries down to CAD 600/month**
   - Current average: **CAD 692**
   - Target savings: **CAD 92/month**
   - How: weekly meal plan, store-brand swaps, bulk staples, and a fixed shopping list to reduce impulse buys.

3. **Hold Utilities + Misc together to CAD 300/month**
   - Current combined average: **CAD 385**
   - Target savings: **CAD 85/month**
   - How: lower heating/cooling use, cut standby power, and set a hard discretionary cap for non-essential purchases.

**Combined savings:** **CAD 312/month**
**Budget impact:** **about 8.1% reduction** in total monthly spend

## Volatility Check

- **Most unusually volatile category:** **Misc**
  - It moves **150 → 160 → 155 → 170 → 165 → 180**, which is choppy relative to its size and lacks a clear pattern.
  - Small categories can look especially volatile because even CAD 10–30 swings are a large percentage of the line item.
- **Fastest upward pressure:** **Eating out**
  - It rises steadily every month, so it is less “erratic” than misc, but it is the **most concerning trend** because the growth is persistent.

If you want, I can also turn this into a **one-page budget dashboard** with percentages, category shares, and a simple savings target.

## Offer Snapshot for WLB + Learning

**Recommendation:** **C) Hyderabad** is the best overall fit for your stated weighting. It has the strongest estimated first-year pay, much better commute than Bangalore, and a solid balance of stable-company learning without the evening-call risk of the startup.

## Side-by-Side Offer Comparison

**Estimated first-year compensation = base + annual bonus + year-1 joining bonus + year-1 vested stock**
(Stock is assumed to vest evenly over 4 years; taxes, PF, and other deductions not included.)

| Rank | Offer | First-year compensation | Work-life balance | Growth / learning | Commute | Weighted fit | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **Hyderabad (C)** | **₹27.59 LPA** | Good: 2 days/week in office | Strong: established product company | Best practical commute after remote | **8.4 / 10** | Slightly lower learning intensity than a startup |
| 2 | **Pune (B)** | **₹24.15 LPA** | Best on paper, but occasional evening calls | Highest learning upside | Excellent: fully remote | **8.1 / 10** | Lower pay and startup unpredictability |
| 3 | **Bangalore (A)** | **₹27.40 LPA** | Weakest: 3 days/week + 45-min commute | Good: fintech product exposure | Worst commute | **6.9 / 10** | Commute and office load hurt balance |

## Main Trade-offs That Matter

- **If you want the best balance of pay + lifestyle:** **Hyderabad (C)** wins.
- **If you want maximum flexibility and can tolerate occasional late calls:** **Pune (B)** is the strongest pure WLB option.
- **If you want fintech domain exposure and don’t mind commuting:** **Bangalore (A)** is still strong financially, but it loses on day-to-day ease.

## Best Fit by Priority

- **Best overall for your weights:** **C) Hyderabad**
- **Best for pure work-life balance:** **B) Pune**
- **Best for domain-specific learning with a commute cost:** **A) Bangalore**

## Sources

Not needed — this comparison is based on the offer details you provided and a standard year-1 compensation estimate.

## Monthly Budget Snapshot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calculator.svg

Your budget shows a **healthy monthly surplus**. If you save all of it each month, you can build the emergency fund in a little under 5 months.

## Income, Expenses, and Emergency Fund Runway

**KPI lines**
- **Total monthly income:** $5,150
- **Total monthly expenses:** $3,308
- **Net surplus:** $1,842
- **Savings rate:** **35.8%**
- **Time to $8,500 emergency fund:** **4.62 months**
  Rounded up for whole months: **5 months**

**Formula:**
`Surplus = Income - Expenses`
`Savings rate = Surplus / Income × 100`
`Months to goal = 8,500 / Surplus`

### Variable Check
| Variable | Description | Value |
|---|---|---:|
| I | Total monthly income | $5,150 |
| E | Total monthly expenses | $3,308 |
| S | Monthly surplus available to save | $1,842 |
| R | Savings rate | 35.8% |

| Category | Items | Monthly Total |
|---|---|---:|
| Income | Salary, freelance work, child support | $5,150 |
| Essential expenses | Rent, groceries, utilities, transport, insurance, phone, student loan | $2,935 |
| Flexible expenses | Subscriptions, dining out, miscellaneous | $373 |
| Total expenses | All listed expenses | $3,308 |
| Net surplus | Income minus expenses | $1,842 |

### What this means
- At your current pace, you would reach **$8,500 in about 4 months and 18 days**.
- If you want a cushion for surprise costs, keeping the full surplus in savings each month is a strong plan.
- If you want, I can also turn this into a **50/30/20-style budget** or show how long it takes to reach **$10,000** instead.

response_text:
# Photosynthesis Made Simple

Photosynthesis is how plants make their own food using **sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide**.
In simple terms: plants use energy from the sun to turn **water + air** into **sugar** they can use for growth, and they release **oxygen** into the air.

**Big idea:**
- **Leaves** are the plant’s food-making factories
- **Chlorophyll** is the green pigment that catches sunlight
- The plant uses the sun’s energy to make **glucose**
- **Oxygen** is a helpful byproduct that we breathe

## 45-Minute Mini Lesson Plan

| Step | Time | Focus | Teacher Move | Check for Understanding |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 min | Hook | Ask: “How do plants eat if they don’t have mouths?” | Students share ideas |
| 2 | 10 min | Core idea | Explain sunlight, water, carbon dioxide, glucose, oxygen | Students label a simple diagram |
| 3 | 10 min | Parts of the leaf | Show stomata, chlorophyll, chloroplasts | Students match each part to its job |
| 4 | 10 min | Process practice | Walk through the equation in words and symbols | Students explain the process aloud |
| 5 | 10 min | Review and quiz | Quick recap + 5 practice questions | Exit ticket or oral responses |

## Misconceptions to Clear Up

- **“Plants get their food from soil.”**
  Not exactly. Soil gives plants **water and minerals**, but the plant makes its own food in the leaves.

- **“Plants only do photosynthesis in the daytime.”**
  Photosynthesis needs **light**, so it happens mostly when sunlight is available.

- **“Plants give off oxygen because they breathe like animals.”**
  Plants do use oxygen for respiration, but during photosynthesis they also **release oxygen** as a byproduct.

## Practice Questions with Answers

1. **What is photosynthesis?**
   **Answer:** Photosynthesis is the process plants use to make food from sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.

2. **What three things do plants need for photosynthesis?**
   **Answer:** Sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.

3. **What is the main food made by the plant?**
   **Answer:** Glucose, a type of sugar.

4. **Why are leaves important in photosynthesis?**
   **Answer:** Leaves contain chlorophyll and chloroplasts, which help capture sunlight and make food.

5. **What gas do plants release during photosynthesis?**
   **Answer:** Oxygen.

## Helpful Biology Resources

- **Photosynthesis overview:** https://www.britannica.com/science/photosynthesis
- **Student-friendly explanation:** https://www.khanacademy.org/science/biology/photosynthesis-in-plants
- **Easy revision notes:** https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/topics/zvrrd2p

If you want, I can also turn this into a **45-minute lesson script** or a **one-page student handout**.

response_text:
# Overview

LedgerLite is a small command-line app for tracking personal income and expenses from a local CSV file. It helps you:

- import bank or card transactions
- view spending by category for a month
- export your ledger as JSON for backup or other tools

It is designed for people who are comfortable using a terminal and want a simple, local-first workflow.

# Installation

1. Download or build LedgerLite for your system.
2. Make sure the `ledgerlite` command is available in your terminal.
3. Create a CSV file with these columns: `date`, `description`, `category`, `amount`.

If you already have the app installed, you can start using it right away.

# Quick Start

Import transactions from a CSV file:

`ledgerlite import transactions.csv`

Check totals by category for a month:

`ledgerlite summary --month YYYY-MM`

Export your current ledger to JSON:

`ledgerlite export --format json`

Common uses:

- importing last month’s bank transactions
- checking where money went by category
- exporting data for backup

# Configuration

LedgerLite reads settings from `~/.ledgerlite/config.toml`.

Available options:

- `currency = "USD"` — the currency shown in reports
- `date_format = "YYYY-MM-DD"` — the date format expected in your CSV file
- `default_category = "Uncategorized"` — used when a transaction has no category

A simple config file might look like:

`currency = "USD"`
`date_format = "YYYY-MM-DD"`
`default_category = "Uncategorized"`

# Troubleshooting

- **File not found**
  The CSV path is probably wrong. Check the filename and folder location.

- **Invalid date format**
  The `date` column in your CSV must match the date format in your config file.

- **Permission denied**
  The config file or target folder may not be writable. Try saving it somewhere you have access to.

# FAQ

**What kind of file does LedgerLite import?**
A local CSV file with `date`, `description`, `category`, and `amount` columns.

**Can I change the currency?**
Yes. Set `currency` in `~/.ledgerlite/config.toml`.

**What happens if a category is missing?**
LedgerLite uses `Uncategorized` by default.

**Can I back up my data?**
Yes. Use `ledgerlite export --format json` to save your current ledger in JSON format.

# Best Low-CPU Offline Player for Windows 11
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

For local **MP4/MKV** playback with **SRT** subtitles on an 8 GB Windows 11 laptop, **mpv** is the best pick for the lowest CPU use.
If you want the easiest built-in subtitle timing and audio equalizer controls, **VLC** is the most convenient fallback.

## Player Comparison and Best Pick

| Player | Low CPU use | Subtitle sync | Audio equalizer | Best fit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **mpv** | Excellent | Good | Limited / custom | Lowest overhead for 1080p and 4K playback |
| **MPC-HC** | Very good | Very good | Basic / external filters | Lightweight Windows-style player |
| **VLC** | Good | Excellent | Excellent | Easiest all-in-one setup |

Option 1: **mpv** | Best raw performance for local video playback and the lightest CPU load. | Leanest choice
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/play-circle.svg
Action: [Button: Get mpv](https://mpv.io/installation/)

Option 2: **VLC** | Slightly heavier, but the simplest for subtitle sync and equalizer tuning. | Best controls
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/sliders.svg
Action: [Button: Get VLC](https://www.videolan.org/vlc/)

## Subtitle Sync and Audio EQ Setup

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/gear.svg

- Put the subtitle file next to the video and keep the same base name, for example `Movie.mkv` + `Movie.srt`.
- Open the video in **VLC**.
- For subtitle timing, go to **Tools > Track Synchronization** and adjust the **Subtitle track synchronization** value a little at a time until the text matches speech.
- For the audio equalizer, go to **Tools > Effects and Filters > Audio Effects > Equalizer**.
- Turn on the equalizer, choose a preset, then fine-tune the bands if voices sound too thin, harsh, or boomy.
- If the settings sound right, keep them as your default profile for future files.

## Playback Stutter Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

| Step | Action | What to Check | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Enable hardware-accelerated decoding | Player settings should use GPU decode instead of full CPU decode | CPU load drops and playback smooths out |
| 2 | Test the same file with subtitles off | Subtitle rendering may be causing the lag | If stutter stops, subtitle processing is the issue |
| 3 | Disable extra effects temporarily | Equalizer or filters can add overhead | Playback becomes smoother |
| 4 | Close heavy background apps | Browser tabs, updates, and sync tools can steal CPU/RAM | Fewer dropped frames |
| 5 | Set Windows power mode to Best performance | Laptop throttling can hurt 4K playback | More stable frame delivery |
| 6 | Try a different player on the same file | File codec or render path may suit one player better | You identify whether the issue is the file or the player |

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Download mpv](https://mpv.io/installation/)
Action: [Button: Download VLC](https://www.videolan.org/vlc/)
Action: [Button: MPC-HC releases](https://github.com/clsid2/mpc-hc/releases)

## Sources
- mpv installation: https://mpv.io/installation/
- VLC downloads: https://www.videolan.org/vlc/
- MPC-HC releases: https://github.com/clsid2/mpc-hc/releases

response_text:
# Dark QR Scanner Screen

A clean, dark, one-handed QR scanner for retail use, optimized for fast recognition and easy use in bright outdoor lighting. The layout keeps the camera dominant, moves controls to the lower reach zone, and uses a high-contrast scan frame for instant focus.

## One-Handed Layout Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

- **Top bar:** back button, short title, and a subtle status label.
- **Center:** large camera viewport with a scan frame sized for quick alignment.
- **Lower dock:** torch, image import, and manual entry, all within thumb reach.
- **Bottom sheet:** decoded content preview slides up without blocking the camera.
- **History strip:** compact recent scans row sits just above the gesture area.

## Scanner State Set

### 1) Camera Permission Request

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/camera-video.svg

- Use a clear headline: **“Camera access needed to scan QR codes.”**
- Show one primary action: **Allow Camera**.
- Add a secondary option: **Enter Code Manually**.
- Include a short privacy note and a faint scan frame preview so the screen still feels useful before access is granted.

### 2) Active Scanner View

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/qr-code-scan.svg

- Keep the camera full-screen with a dark vignette to reduce glare.
- Place an animated scan line inside the frame, moving top to bottom in a smooth loop.
- Use bright corner brackets to show the target area immediately.
- Bottom controls:
  - **Torch toggle**
  - **Image import**
  - **Manual code entry**
- Bottom sheet behavior:
  - Show decoded content preview when a code is detected.
  - Include quick actions: **Copy**, **Open Link**, **Share**.
  - Keep the sheet partially expanded so the camera stays visible.
- Add a subtle haptic pulse and a brief focus ring on successful detection.

### 3) Successful Scan Confirmation

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check-circle.svg

- Replace the scan line with a short success flash and a green confirmation state.
- Expand the bottom sheet to show:
  - decoded value
  - link or item name
  - trust/status label
- Primary next step: **Open Link** or **Proceed** based on content type.
- Keep **Scan Another** visible so users can stay in flow.
- Auto-return to scanner after a short delay if no action is taken.

### 4) Invalid QR Error

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/x-circle.svg

- Keep the background calm and dark; use red only as a focused error accent.
- Show a short message such as **“This code can’t be read”** or **“Unsupported QR content.”**
- Offer quick recovery actions:
  - **Rescan**
  - **Import Image**
  - **Enter Code**
- Add a small helper line for likely causes: blur, glare, low contrast, or damaged print.

### 5) Scan History Preview

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock-history.svg

- Show the last 3 scans in a compact horizontal strip.
- Each item should display:
  - short label
  - time
  - status chip
- Tapping a history item reopens the bottom sheet with **Copy**, **Open Link**, and **Share** actions.
- Keep this section collapsed by default so the camera remains the focus.

## Accessibility for Bright Outdoor Use

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/brightness-high.svg

- Use near-black surfaces with off-white text for strong contrast.
- Keep all key buttons at least **44 px** tall for easy thumb reach.
- Make the scan frame larger and brighter than the surrounding UI.
- Add auto-brightness boost while scanning and a dim overlay around the target box.
- Use short labels, large tap targets, and minimal motion outside the scan line.
- Prefer a single accent color for primary actions so the interface stays calm and readable in sunlight.

response_text:
# Mobile App Launch Health Check

Planned launch is **2026-07-15**. With about **27 days left**, the project is **mostly on track on timing, but not yet launch-ready** because payments and QA still need attention.

## Current Status and Top Priorities

| Area | Status | What it means | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schedule | Slightly at risk | The launch date is still achievable if blockers clear soon | High |
| Design | **90% complete** | Final approvals are the last step before sign-off | Medium |
| Backend | Auth done; payments failing in staging | Core login path is stable, but checkout is a launch blocker | High |
| QA | **60% complete**, **18 bugs open**, **4 high priority** | Test coverage is behind where it should be this close to launch | High |
| Marketing | Approved | Assets are ready and the email campaign is already scheduled for **2026-07-10** | Low |
| Staffing | QA coverage reduced Jul 1–5 | One QA engineer out during a critical finish window | Medium |
| Budget | **$98k spent / $120k total** | **$22k remaining**; spend is high but still manageable if controlled | Medium |

**Verdict:** The launch is **recoverable**, but the critical path is now dominated by **payments stability** and **QA burn-down**.

### Top 3 Next Actions
1. **Fix payments in staging and verify the full checkout flow**
   This is the biggest launch blocker; nothing else matters if payment fails at release.

2. **Burn down the 4 high-priority QA bugs first, then close the remaining defect list**
   Focus on release-blocking issues before the QA engineer is out from **2026-07-01 to 2026-07-05**.

3. **Get final design approvals and set a formal go/no-go checkpoint**
   Lock the UI, confirm launch assets, and use the remaining **$22k** as a guardrail for any last-minute work.

# 72-Hour Self-Care Plan for Cough, Sore Throat, and Low-Grade Fever

With **5 days** of dry cough, sore throat, and a **max temperature of 37.8°C**, this is often managed at home for another **72 hours** if you are breathing comfortably and your asthma is stable. Because you have **mild asthma**, watch closely for any wheeze, chest tightness, or increased inhaler use.

## Next 72 Hours: Practical Plan

| Time window | What to do | Why it helps |
|---|---|---|
| **Today** | Rest, drink fluids regularly, keep taking **cetirizine 10 mg daily** if it helps your allergies, and use **warm drinks / honey** for throat and cough comfort. | Hydration and throat soothing can reduce cough triggers and irritation. |
| **Today** | Use **saline nasal spray or rinse** if you have post-nasal drip, congestion, or throat drainage. | Often helps dry cough from allergies or upper-airway irritation. |
| **Today** | If fever, aches, or throat pain are bothering you, consider an adult pain/fever reliever such as **acetaminophen/paracetamol 500–1000 mg every 6–8 hours as needed**; keep within the label maximum. | Can make you more comfortable while the illness passes. |
| **Tonight** | Sleep with your head slightly elevated; use a **cool-mist humidifier** if air is dry. | Can reduce throat irritation and coughing at night. |
| **Next 24 hours** | If cough feels “tickly” and dry, ask a pharmacist whether a short-term cough suppressant such as **dextromethorphan** is appropriate. | May reduce annoying dry cough, especially at night. |
| **Next 24–48 hours** | If allergy symptoms are prominent, ask about an **intranasal steroid spray** such as **fluticasone** or **mometasone**. | Often better than more antihistamine for post-nasal drip/allergy-driven symptoms. |
| **Next 48–72 hours** | Reassess: if you are clearly improving, continue home care; if you are not improving or are worsening, arrange medical review. | A 5+ day cough with fever should start trending better. |

## Over-the-Counter Options to Discuss With a Pharmacist

- **Acetaminophen/paracetamol**: reasonable for fever, sore throat, body aches.
  - Standard adult example: **500–1000 mg per dose every 6–8 hours as needed**
  - Be careful not to double-dose by taking combo cold/flu products that also contain acetaminophen.

- **Saline nasal spray or nasal rinse**: helpful if allergy/post-nasal drip is contributing.

- **Intranasal corticosteroid spray**: useful if allergies are driving symptoms.
  - Examples: **fluticasone**, **mometasone**
  - These are not instant relief, but they can help over a few days.

- **Dextromethorphan**: may help a **dry, irritating cough** short term.

- **Honey**: a simple option for throat irritation and cough soothing.
  - Do **not** use for infants, but it is generally fine for adults.

- **Throat lozenges / warm salt-water gargles**: good for sore throat comfort.

- **Ibuprofen or naproxen**: only if a pharmacist says it is suitable for you.
  - In some people with asthma, NSAIDs can worsen wheeze or breathing.

## Asthma-Specific Cautions

- **Do not ignore wheeze or chest tightness**, even if the cough seems “just viral” or “allergies.”
- If you have a **rescue inhaler** prescribed, keep it with you and use it **only as directed on your asthma plan**.
- Be cautious with **oral decongestants** such as **pseudoephedrine** or **phenylephrine**: they can cause **jitteriness, fast heart rate, and sleep problems**, and may be a poor fit if you feel unwell.
- Avoid taking **multiple cold/flu combination products** at the same time; they often duplicate ingredients or add sedating antihistamines.
- If you notice that **cetirizine** makes you sleepy or very dry, tell the pharmacist; it can sometimes add to throat dryness.

## Red Flags That Need Urgent Medical Care

Seek urgent care **now** if you develop any of the following:

- **Shortness of breath**, trouble speaking full sentences, or breathing that is getting worse
- **Wheezing or chest tightness** that is new, significant, or not relieved by your usual asthma medicine
- **Blue lips**, marked drowsiness, confusion, or fainting
- **Chest pain**
- **High fever** or fever that is rising, especially with feeling very unwell
- **Severe throat swelling**, drooling, or inability to swallow fluids
- **Coughing up blood**
- **Dehydration**: very dark urine, dizziness, inability to keep fluids down
- **Symptoms worsening after initial improvement**
- **Asthma rescue inhaler needed much more often than usual**

## When to Get Checked Soon, Even If Not Urgent

Arrange a clinician visit in the next day or two if:

- The cough and fever are **not improving after 72 hours**
- You develop **new phlegm**, especially colored sputum with worsening symptoms
- You have **recurrent fevers**
- You have known asthma but are needing your reliever more than usual
- You suspect **COVID-19 or influenza** and want testing or treatment guidance

## Sources

- NHS: Cough and cough self-care — https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cough/
- NHLBI: Asthma basics and warning signs — https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/asthma
- NHS: Asthma symptoms and when to seek help — https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/asthma/

response_text:
# What Your Landlord Text Raises in California

I’m reading this as a normal residential lease in Los Angeles, with only a text message so far and **no emergency**.

- **Entry notice:** In California, a landlord generally needs **advance written notice** and must enter at a **reasonable time** for a valid reason like maintenance.
- **Open-ended access window:** “Any day between 08:00 and 20:00” is very broad. It’s reasonable to ask for a **specific date/time window**.
- **Administrative fee:** A **$150 fee for short-notice access** is a red flag. Ask for the **exact lease clause or legal authority** before agreeing to pay it.
- **Eviction threat by text:** A landlord cannot just “evict” you by text. Eviction normally requires a **formal legal process** and valid grounds.
- **Work-from-home impact:** Working from home does **not** block lawful access, but it does support asking to **schedule entry in advance** and keep it narrow.
- **Paper trail:** Save the text, reply in writing, and keep everything calm and factual.

# Calm, Practical Next Steps

1. **Reply in writing, not by phone.**
   Keep it short: you’re willing to cooperate with lawful entry, but you need proper notice and a specific time.

2. **Do not agree to the fee right away.**
   Ask them to identify the lease section or statute supporting the $150 charge.

3. **Offer a few specific time windows.**
   This keeps you cooperative while protecting your schedule.

4. **Ask for the maintenance reason.**
   Knowing whether it’s routine repair, inspection, or a vendor visit helps you judge whether the request is normal.

5. **Keep the tone non-confrontational.**
   Use words like “please,” “I’m available,” and “to coordinate.”

6. **If they keep threatening eviction or access without proper notice, get help.**
   A local tenant hotline or legal aid group can review the text and your lease.

# Short Email You Can Send

Subject: Maintenance Entry Notice

Hi [Landlord Name],

I’m willing to cooperate with lawful maintenance entry. Please send the required written notice with the specific date, approximate time, and purpose of the visit.

I do not agree to a $150 administrative fee for ordinary maintenance access, and I ask that you remove that charge unless you can point me to the lease provision or legal basis for it.

Please also confirm that any entry will be scheduled at a reasonable time and with proper notice. I’m happy to coordinate a specific window that works for both of us.

Thank you,
[Your Name]

# Quick Actions

Action: [Button: California entry law] https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1954.&lawCode=CIV
Action: [Button: LA tenant help] https://dcba.lacounty.gov/portfolio/landlord-tenants/

# Sources

- California Civil Code § 1954: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1954.&lawCode=CIV
- Los Angeles County tenant/landlord help: https://dcba.lacounty.gov/portfolio/landlord-tenants/
- California Courts self-help, landlord-tenant: https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/landlord-tenant

response_text:
# Porto Family Rental Comparison for September 2026

I ranked these by your priority order: commute, school access, size, elevator, quiet street, and pet-friendliness, while staying within **€1,600/month including HOA**.

## Ranked Fit for Your Priorities

| Rank | Apartment | Fit | Why it stands out | Main drawback |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **A** | **Best overall** | **78 m²**, under budget, **18-minute metro commute**, **600 m to school**, **pet-friendly** | **No elevator** |
| 2 | **B** | **Best building/access** | **84 m²**, exactly at budget, **22-minute metro commute**, **350 m to school**, **elevator** | **Not pet-friendly** |
| 3 | **C** | **Least aligned** | Cheapest at **€1,300**, elevator, pet-friendly | **72 m²** and **30-minute commute** exceed your core limits |

## What Each Option Means for a Family of Three

**A — best balance**
- Checks the most important boxes at once: commute, size, school access, and pets.
- The only major miss is the **lack of elevator**, which matters most if you expect frequent stroller trips, groceries, or future long-term convenience.
- Quietness is unknown, but a 2nd floor can still be workable if the street itself is calm.

**B — strongest if elevator matters more than pets**
- Best fit for **school proximity** and **building convenience**.
- It is the only option with an elevator and the largest floor area.
- The dealbreaker is **no pet-friendly policy**; if you have a pet or plan to get one, this is a hard conflict.

**C — budget-friendly but weakest overall**
- It is the least expensive and has an elevator and pet-friendly rules.
- But it misses your two most important functional targets: **size** and **metro commute**.
- For a family of three, **72 m²** is workable but below your stated minimum, and **30 minutes** to downtown is outside your limit.

## Best Choice for Your Family

**I would choose Apartment A.**

Why:
- It best matches the priorities that affect daily life most: **commute, size, and pet-friendliness**.
- It stays comfortably under budget.
- **78 m²** clears your minimum, and **18 minutes to downtown** gives you room for regular city trips without feeling stretched.

### Trade-off to accept
- You would be giving up the elevator.
- If the elevator is a must-have because of mobility, stroller use, or long-term comfort, then **B becomes the practical second choice** only if the pet rule does not matter.

## Quick Decision

- **Choose A** if you want the strongest overall family fit.
- **Choose B** if elevator access is essential and pets are not part of the plan.
- **Skip C** unless budget is overriding everything else.

# Lisbon Product Ops Transition Plan

Your profile is a good fit for **junior product operations** if you position yourself as an **ops + data + cross-functional support** candidate, not as a pure customer support profile.
Your **€32,000–€38,000 gross** target is realistic for English-first, remote-first SaaS teams in Portugal/Spain, especially when you show strong Excel/SQL work, process ownership, and clear stakeholder communication.

## 10-Week Roadmap and Skill-Gap Matrix

| Skill area | What you already have | Gap to close | 10-week action | Proof to add |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer support intelligence | 6 years in SaaS support; direct user pain points | Translate tickets into product insights | Build a weekly issues-to-insights memo from support themes | 1 insight memo + CV bullet |
| Excel and reporting | Strong Excel | Move from reporting to KPI ownership | Create a simple product ops dashboard with 3 core metrics | Dashboard screenshot + metrics note |
| SQL analysis | Strong SQL | Use SQL for product questions, not just extraction | Write queries for feature usage, churn, and ticket trends | 3 query examples |
| Process and workflow design | Escalations, follow-ups, internal coordination | Document repeatable SOPs and handoffs | Map one support-to-product workflow and write an SOP | SOP + workflow diagram |
| Cross-functional communication | Customer-facing communication | Write concise product-facing updates | Draft launch updates, risk notes, and status summaries | 2 writing samples |
| Automation and data cleanup | Basic Python | Use Python for light leverage, not complexity | Clean exports or automate one recurring report | Simple script or workflow note |
| Product ops language | Real business exposure, but not the title | Learn release, roadmap, intake, and prioritization language | Review 10 job ads and mirror the keywords | Tailored CV + LinkedIn profile |
| Role targeting | Remote-first SaaS awareness | Filter out Spanish-fluent roles | Apply only to English-first jobs; treat Spanish as optional | Target list of 20 companies |

## Skills to Lead With

- **Customer problem detection:** you already know how to spot recurring pain points, edge cases, and broken workflows.
- **Operational ownership:** you can manage queues, escalations, handoffs, follow-ups, and deadlines without losing detail.
- **Excel + SQL analysis:** you can turn messy support data into dashboards, trend reports, and action items.
- **Stakeholder communication:** you can explain problems clearly to customers today; product ops needs that same clarity internally.
- **Process improvement:** you know where work gets stuck and how to tighten it with SOPs, templates, and lightweight automation.
- **English-first positioning:** lead with English working fluency and remote collaboration; list Spanish only as basic/intermediate if true.

## Resume Bullet Rewrites

Use these as templates and swap in your real metrics where you have them.

- Turned recurring customer issues into a weekly **Excel/SQL insights report**, highlighting top ticket drivers and recurring product friction for Product and Support.
- Coordinated **cross-functional escalation workflows** across Support, Product, and Engineering, clarifying ownership and improving handoff speed for complex cases.
- Automated repetitive **reporting and data cleanup** with Excel formulas and basic Python, reducing manual work and improving the consistency of team reports.

## Best-Fit Target Roles

- Product Operations Associate / Specialist
- Product Ops Analyst
- Customer Operations Analyst
- Support Operations Specialist
- GTM / Revenue Operations Analyst at product-led SaaS companies

If you want the fastest path, focus on **product ops-adjacent roles** first: they value your support background, analytics skills, and process thinking more than a traditional entry-level PM track.

response_text:
# Practical Plumber-Hiring Checklist for a Lisbon 3-Bedroom Apartment

Use this when the apartment has **repeated low water pressure** and a **slow kitchen drain**. The goal is to hire someone who diagnoses first, quotes clearly, and avoids unnecessary pipe replacement.

## Most Likely Causes to Diagnose First

- **Low water pressure**
  - Partially closed shutoff valve or meter valve
  - Clogged faucet aerator, shower head, or inline filter
  - Faulty or mis-set pressure reducing valve
  - Corroded/undersized old pipes, especially in older buildings
  - Building-wide supply issue in the riser or shared vertical stack
  - Municipal pressure fluctuation at certain hours

- **Slow kitchen drain**
  - Grease and food buildup in the sink trap or branch line
  - Partially blocked shared waste stack
  - Kinked, poorly sloped, or damaged under-sink piping
  - Air/venting issue causing gurgling and slow emptying
  - Problem deeper in the line if other nearby fixtures also drain slowly

- **If both problems happen together**
  - They may still be unrelated, but a good plumber should test each separately before recommending major work.

## Questions to Ask Before You Book

- Are you able to **diagnose both issues in one visit** and separate apartment-level problems from building-level problems?
- Will you **measure water pressure** at the kitchen tap and, if needed, compare it with other fixtures?
- Will you inspect the **shutoff valves, pressure reducing valve, aerators, and under-sink trap** before suggesting replacement?
- Do you clear kitchen drains with **mechanical cleaning or inspection first**, rather than relying on chemicals?
- What is included in the **call-out fee**, and does it count toward the repair if I approve the work?
- Will you provide a **written quote** with labor, parts, VAT, and any emergency or parking charges listed separately?
- Do you issue an **invoice**, and what warranty do you give on labor and parts?
- If the issue is in a **shared riser or common drain**, will you stop and explain the next step instead of doing unnecessary apartment work?

## Photos and Measurements to Collect

- Clear photo of the **kitchen sink, trap, and all visible piping** under the cabinet
- Photo of the **hot and cold shutoff valves**
- Short video of the **sink draining** from full to empty
- Short video of the **kitchen tap flow** at normal use and at full open
- Photo of any **leaks, corrosion, staining, or mineral buildup**
- Note whether low pressure affects:
  - only the kitchen
  - the whole apartment
  - only hot water
  - only certain times of day

Useful measurements to write down:

- **Fill time** for a 1-liter jug from the kitchen tap
- **Drain time** for a full sink of water
- Apartment **floor level**
- Building **age** if known
- Whether neighbors have the same pressure issue
- Any recent work on the building’s plumbing or water supply

## Fair Quote-Comparison Template

| Item | What to compare | Good quote includes | Warning sign |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial diagnosis | What they will test before repairing | Pressure check, valve review, drain inspection | “We know the fix already” without inspection |
| Low-pressure repair | Whether the root cause is identified | Cleaning, valve adjustment, PRV service, minor part replacement | Immediate full repipe recommendation |
| Slow drain repair | Whether blockage removal is included | Trap cleaning, mechanical clearing, test flush | Chemical treatment only |
| Parts and materials | Brand, size, and necessity | Listed parts with prices | “Materials extra” with no detail |
| Labor and access | Time, call-out, parking, urgency | Hourly rate or fixed labor, all surcharges listed | Hidden fees added later |
| Warranty | What is covered and for how long | Written warranty on labor/parts | No warranty or only verbal promise |

## Red Flags That Point Beyond a Simple Repair

- The plumber blames **“the municipality”** without testing pressure at the apartment
- They want to **replace pipes immediately** without checking valves, aerators, or pressure
- They rely on **chemical drain cleaner** instead of clearing the blockage mechanically
- They refuse to give a **written quote** or itemize labor and parts
- They won’t say whether the issue is **inside the apartment or in a shared building line**
- They recommend a large job after a **very short visit** and no measurements
- They ask for **full cash upfront** or push urgent replacement without evidence
- Multiple fixtures are weak, or the kitchen drain backs up and other drains are also slow, which can mean a **shared stack, venting issue, or deeper pipe problem**

## Helpful Lisbon References

- EPAL, Lisbon water utility: https://www.epal.pt/
- ERSAR, Portuguese water and waste regulator: https://www.ersar.pt/
- Consumer portal, Portugal: https://www.consumidor.gov.pt/

If you want, I can turn this into a **one-page homeowner checklist** you can send directly to plumbers by WhatsApp or email.

response_text:
# Cold-Start Rough Idle: Most Likely Causes for Your Civic

Your pattern points most strongly to a **maintenance/deposit issue**, not a hard failure: brief rough idle only after cold starts, no check-engine light, lower mpg, city driving, and service overdue by 14 months. I’d prioritize the cheapest checks that can also improve reliability for the next year.

## Ranked Likely Causes

1. **Dirty throttle body / intake deposits**
   - Very common with mostly city use.
   - Can cause a shaky idle for the first 10–15 seconds after startup and hurt mpg.

2. **Aging spark plugs or a weak coil/boot**
   - At **98,500 miles**, plugs are a prime suspect if they’ve never been replaced.
   - Mild misfire can happen without turning on the CEL.

3. **Restricted engine air filter or intake leak**
   - A clogged filter, loose clamp, cracked intake tube, or small vacuum leak can upset cold idle and fuel trims.

4. **PCV valve issue or crankcase ventilation problem**
   - A sticking PCV valve can create rough idle and extra oil consumption/fuel-trim drift.

5. **Fuel injector deposits / fuel delivery imbalance**
   - More likely on a city-driven car that rarely gets long, steady highway runs.
   - Often shows up as worse mileage before any warning light appears.

## First Five Checks and Repairs in Order

| Step | Action | What to Check | Expected Result | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scan for pending codes and misfire counts | Pending P-codes, fuel trims, misfire counters, battery voltage | Confirms whether the rough idle is real misfire vs. normal cold-start behavior | DIY-friendly |
| 2 | Inspect/replace engine air filter and check intake tubing | Dirty filter, loose clamps, cracked boot, split vacuum hose | Restores airflow and rules out an easy air leak | DIY-friendly |
| 3 | Clean the throttle body | Carbon buildup on throttle plate/bore; do an idle relearn if needed | Smoother cold idle and often better mpg | DIY-friendly |
| 4 | Inspect and likely replace spark plugs; inspect coil boots | Plug wear, oil fouling, carbon tracking, cracked boots | Best chance to fix brief rough idle at this mileage | DIY-friendly if you’re comfortable; otherwise shop |
| 5 | Test PCV valve and, if still rough, do a smoke test / injector check | PCV flow, vacuum leaks, injector balance, fuel trims under cold start | Finds issues that aren’t obvious visually | Shop-only |

## DIY-Friendly Repairs vs Shop-Only Jobs

**Good DIY candidates**
- Scan for pending codes with a basic OBD-II reader
- Replace the engine air filter
- Inspect intake tubes/clamps and obvious vacuum hoses
- Clean the throttle body carefully
- Replace spark plugs if you have basic tools and torque specs

**Best left to a shop**
- Smoke test for small vacuum leaks
- Injector balance testing / advanced fuel-system diagnosis
- Coil pack diagnosis under load if plugs don’t solve it
- Any repair that requires deep intake disassembly or access you’re not comfortable with

## When to Stop Driving Until It’s Checked

Stop driving and get it inspected soon if you notice any of these:

- **Flashing check-engine light**
- **Rough idle that gets worse or doesn’t clear after warm-up**
- **Stalling at stops, creeping, or in gear**
- **Noticeable loss of power under acceleration**
- **Strong fuel smell, raw exhaust smell, or visible smoke**
- **Engine knocking, pinging, or loud metallic noises**
- **Overheating, coolant warning, or temperature gauge rising**
- **Oil pressure light or charging/battery light coming on**
- **Vibration so severe the car shakes in gear**

For a **60-mile daily commute**, a rough idle that stays mild and only happens briefly after a cold start is usually still drivable, but I would **not** ignore it for a year. The safest plan is to fix the likely basics now and keep a reserve for diagnostics if the first round doesn’t solve it.

## Sources

- Honda Owners manuals and vehicle information: https://owners.honda.com/vehicle-information/information/2017/Civic-sedan/manuals

response_text:
# Three-Course Vegetarian Dinner for 6

A cozy, Valentine-friendly menu that stays **gluten-free, nut-free, under $90**, and doable in **under 2 hours** with just an oven, stovetop, blender, and one large pot.
Use **certified gluten-free stock and chocolate** to keep the whole menu safe.

## Menu at a Glance

**Starter: Roasted tomato & red pepper soup**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Silky, bright, and easy to batch in the blender
- Finished with basil oil and black pepper
- Time: about 30 minutes

**Main: Creamy mushroom, pea & spinach risotto**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/egg-fried.svg
- Rich and festive without needing special equipment
- Naturally gluten-free and easy to scale for 6
- Time: about 35 minutes

**Dessert: Flourless chocolate-orange cake with whipped cream and berries**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cake2.svg
- Elegant, make-ahead friendly, and nut-free
- Deep chocolate flavor with a fresh citrus finish
- Time: about 45 minutes including baking and cooling

## Shopping List

| Ingredient | Approx. quantity | Used for |
|---|---:|---|
| Canned whole tomatoes | 800 g | Soup |
| Roasted red peppers, drained | 250 g | Soup |
| Yellow onions | 3 medium, about 450 g | Soup, risotto |
| Carrots | 2 medium, about 180 g | Soup |
| Garlic | 2 bulbs, about 60 g | Soup, risotto |
| Fresh basil | 20 g | Soup garnish |
| Arborio rice | 500 g | Risotto |
| Mushrooms | 500 g | Risotto |
| Frozen peas | 300 g | Risotto |
| Baby spinach | 200 g | Risotto |
| Vegetable stock | 2 L | Soup, risotto |
| Parmesan | 150 g | Risotto |
| Lemon | 1 | Risotto |
| Eggs | 6 | Cake |
| Dark chocolate | 250 g | Cake |
| Butter | 160 g | Cake |
| Sugar | 170 g | Cake, cream |
| Cocoa powder | 25 g | Cake |
| Orange | 1 | Cake |
| Double cream | 250 ml | Cake topping |
| Mixed berries | 300 g | Cake topping |
| Olive oil | 100 ml | Soup, risotto |
| Vanilla extract | 5 ml | Cake |
| Cannellini beans | 1 can, 400 g | Protein swap option |

**Estimated total:** about **$70–$80**, depending on your store and whether you already have oil, salt, pepper, sugar, and vanilla.

## Prep Timeline for One Person

1. **0:00–0:10**
   Preheat the oven to **180°C**. Line and mix the chocolate cake batter first, then get it into the oven.

2. **0:10–0:15**
   While the cake bakes, chop the soup vegetables: onion, carrots, garlic, and peppers.

3. **0:15–0:35**
   Make the soup in the large pot: sauté onion, carrot, and garlic; add tomatoes, roasted peppers, and stock; simmer, then blend until smooth. Keep warm.

4. **0:35–0:45**
   Remove cake from the oven and let it cool. Rinse the pot and prep risotto ingredients: finely chop onion, slice mushrooms, measure rice, stock, peas, spinach, and parmesan.

5. **0:45–1:20**
   Cook the risotto in the same pot: soften onion, brown mushrooms, stir in rice, then add hot stock gradually. Stir in peas, spinach, lemon zest, and parmesan at the end.

6. **1:20–1:30**
   Taste and adjust seasoning on the soup and risotto. Whip the cream and set out the berries.

7. **1:30–1:40**
   Serve the **starter**. Keep the main warm with the lid on and low heat if needed.

8. **1:40–1:50**
   Serve the **main course**.

9. **1:50–2:00**
   Slice the cake, top with cream and berries, and serve dessert.

## Protein-Boost Swaps

- **Tofu topper for the main:** Cube **300 g extra-firm tofu**, season with salt, pepper, and paprika, then roast or pan-brown it. Add it on top of the risotto for a bigger protein hit.
- **Bean boost for the starter or main:** Stir **250 g drained cannellini beans** into the soup or fold them into the risotto near the end for extra protein and a creamier texture.

If you want, I can turn this into a **minute-by-minute cooking checklist** or a **plated serving guide for a romantic table setup**.
